summary: Slow start (left around 9am) after a rest-plus-learning-festival stretch, then a short flat 52-mile ride to Murphysboro IL with many detours: a pet rescue thrift store, a BBQ shop, an art store, a cafe and an antique store. The group rode the last 20 miles at about 18 mph.
slept_at: Jessica's place, Murphysboro IL (Warmshowers host)
contacts: Sherie and Brad (hosts, Harrisburg IL): blueberry french toast casserole breakfast
Jessica (Warmshowers host, Murphysboro IL): dog Echo, watermelon
Meliah (Little Egypt Art Association, IL; town not stated): recommended a nearby cafe and a bathroom stop
planning_notes: Harrisburg IL BBQ shop sold pork steaks at $7.99/lb and whole racks of ribs at $19.99 (cheap meat stop).
Team morning routine slipped from a 6am wake and 8am leave to a 9am departure after a rest and learning-festival double day; re-commit to early starts right after rest days.

summary: First century (101.1 miles) from Murphysboro IL to St. Louis MO, leaving by 7am, a team record start. Rest stops at a Lutheran church, a Dairy Queen and a coffee shop; the last stretch ran on the paved Metro Bike Link Trail past the Gateway Arch.
slept_at: Alex's second apartment, St. Louis MO (host Alexander)
contacts: Jessica (Warmshowers host, Murphysboro IL): eggs and pancakes before the century
St Luke's Lutheran Church (first rest stop; town not stated): took photos for their monthly newsletter
Alexander and his wife (host, St. Louis MO): lasagna and cookies
Marvelin Higginbottom (MIT Edgerton Center contact)
planning_notes: Metro Bike Link Trail is paved and scenic into downtown St. Louis.
Crossing the main bridge into St. Louis with cars right beside the riders was scary; look for a safer approach or a path.
Chamois butter reapplied behind a building at the third rest stop prevented saddle chafing on century day.
A tailwind made the century much faster than usual; plan for days when the wind is in your favor.
MIT auditors reviewing team transactions added friction; keep receipts and transaction records organized as you go.

summary: Morning in St. Louis with a Forest Park tour from host Alex, then a Missouri ride on the Katy Trail. Caroline SAG'd out with an elbow nerve injury; a storm stranded the group near Augusta MO for about two hours, and Nate SAG'd the rest of the team to a pizza dinner and an Airbnb on the Katy Trail.
slept_at: Airbnb along the Katy Trail (donated by Kate Engelmann)
contacts: Alex (host, St. Louis MO): tour of Forest Park and a coffee stop at Kaldi's
Kate Engelmann (donated the Katy Trail Airbnb)
planning_notes: Katy Trail is a 240-mile rail trail across Missouri, good for steady riding; plan trailhead rest stops along it.
Augusta MO (Katy Trail trailhead): the town is mostly abandoned storefronts with rotten floors. One rider fell through a floor of the 'HOSTEL' building, so do not enter abandoned buildings.
Afternoon thunderstorms on the Katy Trail forced a roughly two-hour shelter. Have a bail-out plan and a SAG driver for storm days.
Philly's Pizza in Marthasville MO was one of the best pizzas of the trip.
Sophia M. Sach's Butterfly House near St. Louis: a fun first rest stop, with a snow cone truck and a carousel.
Numbness in the pinky that spread up the arm to the elbow was serious enough to force a SAG; do not push through nerve symptoms.

summary: Caroline took a rest day for her elbow and Nunu went to urgent care in Jefferson City for chafing, so three bikes went on a weak hitch. Drew's tire was slashed; the team put a wheel from Caroline's unused bike on his bike and took the damaged wheel to a bike shop before it closed. The group reached Vince's in Columbia MO at 9pm.
slept_at: Vince's house, Columbia MO (Warmshowers host)
contacts: Vince (Warmshowers host, Columbia MO): reheated lasagna and shared local ice cream
Unnamed bike shop (name and town not stated) that had the exact tire needed
planning_notes: Hermann MO Airbnb: the gravel driveway turned to wet mud and the car got stuck; it took a push and a little gas to get out.
Stomp'n Grounds Espresso Bar in Hermann MO: a coffee stop on the drive.
The hitch struggled with three bikes; a team of seven needs more rack capacity for days when several riders are off the bike.
Carry a spare tire or wheel. A slashed tire could not be patched, so the team borrowed a wheel from an idle bike.
Call ahead to a bike shop in the next city to confirm the exact tire size, and get the wheel there before it closes.

summary: Carmen reflects on the team's 'speed demon vs sidequester' split and argues for balance. The group took a long sidequest (peaches, an art gallery, a casino stop and a Boonville festival), then rode into a storm, and a collision between Nunu and Nate at a turn broke two screens. They ended at Dave and Shandra's house in Marshall MO.
slept_at: Dave and Shandra's house, Marshall MO (host)
contacts: Dave and Shandra (host, Marshall MO): iced tea, dinner, and an early 5am breakfast; they had read the team's blogs; dog Percy
planning_notes: Boonville MO has an annual festival with a quilting circle and a vintage car show; worth a stop if your dates line up.
Fresh peach stand on the way out of Columbia MO: a great sidequest, but keep the time budget in mind.
Katy Trail: RV drivers passed with about a foot of room; ride single file and be ready to pull off.
Dave and Shandra offered a 5am breakfast for an early start; ask hosts about early breakfasts before hot days.
Nunu missed a turn and Nate ran into her; keep spacing and call out turns in a group.

summary: Forecast of 107-degree 'feels like' heat and 30 mph crosswinds led to a 4am wake and a 5:30am start on a route with about 5,000 ft of climbing, which was not flat as they expected. The double draft line broke on the climbs and the team was exhausted at the second rest stop. They reached a Kansas City hotel around 3pm.
slept_at: Hotel in downtown Kansas City MO (name not stated)
contacts: Dave and Shandra (host, Marshall MO): breakfast before the 5am departure; puppy Percy
planning_notes: The Marshall to Kansas City route showed about 5,000 ft of climbing, not flat; check the elevation profile before trusting that Missouri is flat.
Cooling towels did not help in 100-degree heat.
On steep climbs the double draft line breaks up; plan a single line and regroup at each climb.
On extreme heat days, leave by about 5am and aim to finish before noon.

summary: Rest day in Kansas City: a hotel breakfast, a Barnes and Noble stop, Shake Shack, Auntie Anne's, a free yoga class arranged by Aarushi, and a Netherlands vs Morocco World Cup watch party that ended in a penalty shootout loss for the Netherlands.
slept_at: Hotel in Kansas City MO (name not stated)
contacts: CorePower Yoga, Kansas City MO: free beginner class and loaned yoga clothes (arranged by Aarushi)
planning_notes: CorePower Yoga in Kansas City offered a free beginner class and lent apparel; ask local studios about free team classes on rest days.
Kansas City had World Cup watch parties during the 2026 tournament.

summary: Learning festival at aSTEAM Village in Kansas City MO drew only 15 students, far below the usual 60 to 80. The team then ran a mini-LF for an absent student, ate at Joe's BBQ near a World Cup watch party, and spent the night at a laundromat that was an ordeal with the tents.
slept_at: Hotel provided by aSTEAM Village, Kansas City MO
learning_festival: aSTEAM Village, Kansas City MO: 15 students (usual 60 to 80). Workshops: electric motor with electromagnet (Nate and Drew), iodine clock chemistry (Carmen and Aarushi), 2D-to-3D design (Nunu and Caroline), and a motion-sensing light circuit (Tatiana). Mini-LF for one absent student afterward.
contacts: aSTEAM Village (LF host program; provided the hotel)
Amelia Alinkil (helped develop the circuits workshop; founding member of Yuva Impact)
planning_notes: Joe's BBQ in Kansas City (near the Power and Light District) was the team's favorite meal of the trip; its patio sits next to the watch party crowd.

Kansas City laundromat cost $8.50 per machine. Sleeping bags and tents took over an hour to wash; the owner warned tents would melt on heat, and the team's tents came out dry on medium heat, so ask staff before drying.
LF turnout dropped to 15 students; confirm registrations with the host before the event.
Plan laundry for a day the car is free; the team had three days of dirty clothes.

summary: Crossed into Kansas, rode through Kansas City's quieter west side, and detoured around a road closure using the square road grid. Tatiana and Caroline each got a flat on gravel, the team skipped the last rest stop, and Tatiana bonked before reaching Scott's house in Overbrook KS for burgers and pickleball.
slept_at: Scott's house, Overbrook KS (host)
contacts: Scott (host, Overbrook KS): owns a retirement community, took the team to a tavern and to pickleball
Trek bike shop, Lawrence KS: Nunu found it while looking for postcards; it could fix the tires
planning_notes: Kansas gravel roads produced two flats in one day; carry two spare tubes and a patch kit.
Kansas road closures: the square mile grid makes detours easy (take the next road over, then turn back).
Vinland Valley Nursery (near the route in Kansas): family-owned, with pick-your-own flowers, ceramics, a coffee shop and iced drinks.
Overbrook KS tavern is known for burgers; ask your host.
Skipping lunch on a 4am start led to a bonk; always pack food for the middle of the day.

summary: Breakfast with the retirees at Scott's Overbrook community, then a flat-tire day: the team logged seven flats in about 24 hours, including Caroline's, Carmen's twice, and a passing cyclist's tire. After Osage City stops they rode a headwind slog to 12th Avenue Baptist Church in Emporia KS.
slept_at: 12th Avenue Baptist Church, Emporia KS (Pastor Brett)
contacts: Scott (host, Overbrook KS): breakfast at his retirement community
Vickie (Didde Catholic Campus Center, Emporia KS): helped find housing
Pastor Brett (12th Avenue Baptist Church, Emporia KS): hosted the team
Diane and Elaine (Didde Catholic Campus Center, Emporia KS): warm dinner on arrival
planning_notes: Osage City KS: downtown was closed; the grocery store was the only resupply stop.
Gravel and tubeless tires near Osage City: many punctures. Keep riding after a puncture so the sealant can seal it, and carry spares.
Didde Catholic Campus Center in Emporia KS helps find cyclist housing; contact Vickie.
Afternoon headwinds slowed the last 60 percent of the route; start earlier on Kansas days.

summary: Snooze-heavy late start (about 9:40am) and a ride on US-50 with its wide shoulder. Stops included HeBrews CoffeeHouse in Cottonwood Falls, a minivan oil pan that dragged until a free fix, and a giant nail puncture on Aarushi's tire at a Dollar General before the group reached Janet and Orvin's in Newton KS.
slept_at: Janet and Orvin's house, Newton KS (Warmshowers hosts)
contacts: Janet and Orvin (Warmshowers hosts, Newton KS): corn on the cob, mulberry rhubarb pie; dog Enzo and cat Phoebe
Vonda (barista, HeBrews CoffeeHouse, Cottonwood Falls KS): donated pastries
Dieker Oil (auto shop near Cottonwood Falls KS): fixed the minivan oil pan for free
planning_notes: US-50 in Kansas has a big shoulder, but semis pass close and some drivers pull fully into the oncoming lane. Gusts push riders sideways.
HeBrews CoffeeHouse in Cottonwood Falls KS is a coffee house and a place of worship; a good rest stop with a courthouse nearby.
Dollar General stops on US-50 are the only shade and snack options on some legs.
A giant nail through a tubeless tire was fixed with gorilla tape and a tube (Nate, at the host's house).
Watch for dogs on the road near the end of the day (Kansas).

summary: July 4 ride starting at 5am to beat 95-degree heat. The group shelter-stopped for about two hours at a Burrton KS gas station during a thunderstorm, then reached a Macksville KS church, after riding 92.6 miles on US-50 with a sandy stretch and cow fields.
slept_at: Church in Macksville KS (contact Katrina)
contacts: Katrina (church contact, Macksville KS): arranged the church stay and told them about the July 4 event in Lewis
Owners of the Oasis gas station (Kansas; names not stated): recently renovated, friendly, sold cold drinks
planning_notes: Burrton KS gas station: a shelter during a storm, with snacks and cold drinks.
Kansas roadside restrooms along US-50 were clean and well kept.
A sandy stretch in Kansas took several miles to cross; plan extra time.
July 4 fireworks in Lewis KS were huge; bring bug spray because mosquitoes and biting flies were heavy in the evening.
Start at 5am on hot days to ride before the heat peaks.

summary: Mosquito-bitten team had breakfast with the Macksville Christian Church community, then rode 62.6 miles with tailwinds past hundreds of windmills and a halfway-point museum to Dodge City KS. Lunch ran from 4pm to 6pm and dinner with hosts Lindy and Warren was around 9pm.
slept_at: Lindy and Warren's house, Dodge City KS (host)
contacts: Lindy and Warren (hosts, Dodge City KS): lasagna and the history of 'Wickedest Little City in America'
Pastor Russell (Macksville Christian Church, KS): hosted a community breakfast
planning_notes: Food: in one day the team ate about 30 Capri Suns, 90 pepperoni slices, 3.5 lb grapefruit, 2.25 lb gummy worms and 2 trays of watermelon. Budget for about double the usual snacks on Kansas days.
Lunch ran from 4pm to 6pm; a long lunch cut into daylight. Keep rest stops short when the day is long.
Bring bug spray for the evening in Kansas; mosquitoes bit the whole team at a park fireworks show.
Windmills near Dodge City gave a strong tailwind for much of the ride.
A halfway-point museum sits between New York and San Francisco; it is not the geographic center, but it has an old single-speed bike on display.

summary: A strong tailwind out of Dodge City made for fast riding. Aarushi's tube-equipped tire flatted again on US-50, so the team took a sandy gravel alternate route to avoid feedlots, and finished at a public pool outside Garden City before dinner at Victory Baptist Church in Lakin KS.
slept_at: Rooms at the local inn, Lakin KS (arranged by Victory Baptist Church)
contacts: Victory Baptist Church, Lakin KS: homemade sloppy joes and ice cream, and arranged rooms at the local inn
planning_notes: Tube-equipped tires went flat repeatedly; carry two or three spare tubes (Nate's advice).
US-50 cattle feedlots next to the road smell horrendous. Prefer the gravel alternate when it is offered.
Public pool outside Garden City KS: a good rest stop on hot days.
A wind turbine assembly factory near Dodge City has blades visible from the road.

summary: Crossed into Colorado and rode a tailwind to Lamar. The lunch rest stop near the state line had aggressive flies, and a nap there turned into a 1.5-hour sleep. Lamar Christian Church housed them, and Lucy's Tacos donated 7 burritos. A bike lock cable knotted around a front axle had to be cut that night.
slept_at: Lamar Christian Church, Lamar CO (church host)
contacts: Lamar Christian Church, Lamar CO: housing for the night
Lucy's Tacos, Lamar CO: donated 7 burritos for dinner
planning_notes: Eastern Colorado near the state line: flies were aggressive at the lunch rest stop. Eat in the car or in shelter, or pick another spot.
Central and Mountain time zones meet on the route at the Colorado line.
Amache National Historic Site (WWII Japanese internment camp): replicas of the buildings on a roughly 410-acre site, with history worth the stop.
Do not wrap a bike lock cable around a front wheel axle; the team had to bolt-cut the cable.
Strong tailwinds let riders hit 29 mph on the final stretch to Lamar.

summary: Learning festival at the Lamar Community Building with 30 students aged 4 to 15 across four groups, a Rock-Paper-Scissors-Rockstar opener, and a pizza lunch in the gym. The day ended with a steakhouse dinner funded by a $20-per-person credit and a Zumba class, and a Tractor Supply loan of wire cutters fixed the lock cable.
slept_at: Lamar Christian Church (church host)
learning_festival: Lamar Community Building, CO, with director Ethan Settles: 30 students aged 4 to 15 in four age groups. Workshops: Tatiana's magic circuit (tilt switch and copper tape), Aarushi and Carmen's chemistry and biology (Monster Genome, iodine clock), Nate and Drew's electromagnetism, and Nunu and Caroline's design. Pizza lunch in the building's gym.
contacts: Ethan Settles (director, Lamar Community Building, CO): set up the tables and fed the kids pizza
JJ (Tractor Supply, Lamar CO): lent wire cutters after the fire department declined for liability reasons
Lamar steakhouse (name not stated): $20 credit per person for the team's dinner
planning_notes: Planning a learning festival takes hundreds of emails with directors (libraries, jails, community centers). Each host needs infrastructure, food for students, marketing support, registration forms and photo releases.
Registrations for the Lamar LF did not arrive until two days before; ask hosts to push registration earlier.
Community building gym: a good lunch break spot where kids can play while teams eat.
Local restaurants will donate meals. Ask a steakhouse early, and a $20-per-person credit is a realistic ask.
Monster Genome leaves felt scraps everywhere and iodine clock needs one beaker per student; plan extra cleanup time.

summary: Routine-focused post that walks through the team's daily schedule and rest-stop tour: Valley Grocery, a Dairy Queen with Tony's fruit stand, a La Junta public pool, a storm shelter at McDonald's and Wendy's, and Knapps Farm Market in Rocky Ford. The team reached Trinity Lutheran Church in Fowler CO into the sunset after a fourth flat of the trip.
slept_at: Trinity Lutheran Church, Fowler CO (Pastor Josephson)
contacts: Pastor Josephson (Trinity Lutheran Church, Fowler CO): taco bar and corn on the cob dinner
Pastor's friend (Fowler CO): unlocked the high school locker room for gang showers
Brenda and Tom (Tatiana's grandparents): bought snacks and extra melon
Tony's Fresh Fruit Stand (next to the Dairy Queen, Las Animas CO)
Knapps Farm Market (Rocky Ford CO): owner stayed open over an hour past closing
planning_notes: Rest stops are planned about every 20 miles, rounding down. Churches are reliable; Valley Grocery and the Dairy Queen worked well.
Tony's Fresh Fruit Stand (next to the Dairy Queen, Las Animas CO): fresh mango, watermelon, pineapple and cantaloupe, with chamoy and tajin.
La Junta public swimming pool (about 57 miles): a great rest stop with diving boards and water slides.
Knapps Farm Market in Rocky Ford CO has the best melons; call ahead, since the owner stayed open late.
Afternoon storm on the Colorado plains brought sand, gusts and a headwind; McDonald's and Wendy's were shelters about a mile apart.
Fowler: a school locker room can serve as gang showers when the team has one or two showers.

summary: Aarushi shaved miles off the planned route (87.4 miles total), and the team detoured to the Pueblo Weisbrod Aircraft Museum. They crossed a dry stretch with no services, a boarded-up I-25 rest stop and a parallel trail, then ended at In-N-Out and an Airbnb in Colorado Springs shared with Aarushi's family.
slept_at: Airbnb shared with Aarushi's family, Colorado Springs CO
contacts: Pueblo Weisbrod Aircraft Museum (Pueblo CO): a staff tour of the hangar
Aarushi's family (hosts in Colorado Springs): Indian dinner
Grandpa Tom and Grandma Brenda (Tatiana's grandparents): bought cinnamon rolls and fruit
planning_notes: Pueblo Weisbrod Aircraft Museum is about 10 miles off route; the team called it worth the detour, with a guided hangar tour.
A long dry stretch had no open services; the first planned produce stop was closed. Carry food and water for 20-plus miles.
The I-25 freeway rest stop was closed and boarded up; traffic at about 80 mph felt unsafe, so the team used the small parallel trail for a few miles.
Colorado Sno-Balls (CO): a medium snow cone (about $2) is huge and well made.
After a rain shower, the Rockies and rainbows made a great view on the final stretch.

summary: Rest day in Colorado Springs: a home-cooked breakfast, a Pikes Peak drive (about three hours up and down) with a scream from the summit, a Garden of the Gods visit, and a mountain-bike ride at Red Rock Canyon by Drew and Carmen (an optional 9.6-mile ride).
slept_at: Airbnb in Colorado Springs (shared with Aarushi's family)
contacts: The Mehrotras (host family, Colorado Springs): home-cooked breakfast and a cauliflower dinner
planning_notes: Pikes Peak road: switchbacks above tree line have no guardrails. The team removed the car's camper top before the drive because of the wind.
Red Rock Canyon (across from Garden of the Gods) has mountain-bike trails. A Garmin cannot tell the trail junctions apart, so download a trail map or ask locals.
Gravel bikes can ride some mountain-bike trails but not 5-foot drops or steep loose rock; expect to walk those sections.
Rest days were spent riding; schedule a true off-bike day if the team needs recovery.

summary: Left Colorado Springs for a long day into Denver (82.5 miles, 3,707 ft): a lakeside rest stop with volleyball and swimming, a mountain-bike detour through a cow pasture, a tea shop stop, and a flat on a climb. The day ended at MIT and Spokes alum hosts Kate and Manuel's house in Denver.
slept_at: Kate and Manuel's house, Denver CO (MIT and Spokes alum hosts)
contacts: Kate and Manuel (MIT and Spokes alum hosts, Denver CO): pesto pasta, cold grapes, and a team debrief about MIT and Spokes
Abhijeet and Roma (Aarushi's family friends, Colorado): protein smoothies at the last rest stop
planning_notes: Denver has the best bike infrastructure and parks on the route so far, according to the team.
A driver yelled at a rider on a narrow Denver street; expect the occasional hostile driver in city traffic.
A lakeside rest stop on the way out of Colorado Springs has a volleyball net and a swim area.
A front tire punctured on a climb; sealant sprayed from the tire, so keep spinning so it can seal.

summary: Largest climb of the trip so far (about 2,000 ft over 10 miles) out of Golden CO, after a Woody's Pizza lunch and a Clear Creek tubing run. Drew felt sick at the top and the team was winded and nauseated at altitude. The day ended at an Idaho Springs Airbnb after construction closures.
slept_at: Airbnb in Idaho Springs CO (hot tub)
planning_notes: Woody's Pizza in Golden CO has a $18.99 all-you-can-eat pizza buffet, which the team said was a great deal.
Golden coffee shop rest stop: an $8 mason-jar lemonade was overpriced; check menus.
Clear Creek in Golden CO has light rapids where people tube; the team went down three times on an air mattress.
Rockies climbs are long climbs followed by long descents, which feels better than the short steep climbs of the Appalachians.
Construction closures near Idaho Springs: workers let the riders through.
Riders from sea level felt winded and nauseated at the top of the climbs; plan for altitude.

summary: Rest day in Idaho Springs: a white water rafting and kayaking trip about 1.5 hours away (Class 2 rapids, with the kayaks spinning and flipping), a 30-foot cliff jump, and a food hall dinner. In the evening the team spent 2 to 3 hours on expense spreadsheets.
slept_at: Airbnb in Idaho Springs CO (sauna and hot tub)
contacts: Rafting outfitter (name not stated; about 1.5 hours from Idaho Springs)
planning_notes: The outfitter needs at least 7 people to run a trip; the team swapped spots for kayaks, so ask about group minimums and seat options first.
Inflatable kayaks spin easily; paddle backward to steer, and enter drops head-on, not sideways.
Class 5 rapids require strong swimming, and Class 2 is more scenic than thrilling; choose by the group's swimming comfort.
A food hall near the rafting area charged $20 to $25 for a burger and about $6 for an empanada; takeout Chinese food was a cheaper option for the team.
Keep receipts and log expenses daily; the team spent hours reconciling the trip's receipts.

summary: Crossed the Continental Divide over Loveland Pass (about 11,990 ft), with a steep final climb and a fast descent. Ashley and her family joined the team in Keystone. A storm around 8pm forced the group into a SAG, and Drew rode on alone through the storm to Breckenridge, where host Alison hosted dinner.
slept_at: Alison's house, Breckenridge CO (host)
contacts: Alison (host, Breckenridge CO): taco and burrito bar; her husband Phil is on a bike tour
Ashley Fisher and family (Tatiana's friend): joined the ride into Keystone and drove to dinner
Ashley's parents: drove Carmen back to Loveland Pass to retrieve the car
planning_notes: Loveland Pass: the last 4 miles climb about 1,500 ft, and the summit is very windy and high. Plan breaks about every half mile.
Carmen left the car at the top, rode down and back up, and then needed a driver to retrieve the car. Arrange a shuttle car in advance.
Afternoon storms over the Colorado passes around Keystone brought lightning. Start early enough to finish before the afternoon storms.
A small SUV could not fit a bike with the front wheel on; the team removed the front wheel.
Drew felt altitude sickness at the summit; eat and drink early on high climbs.

summary: A 105.7-mile day from Breckenridge to Glenwood Springs CO, documented with a photo every 10 minutes. The scenery moved from mountains to canyon to desert, and the drivers switched at 2pm.
planning_notes: Breckenridge to Glenwood Springs goes from mountains to canyon to desert in one day, so pack for changing temperatures and terrain.
A 105-mile day with a driver switch around 2pm kept the riders moving; plan driver swaps for long days.

summary: Learning festival at the Glenwood Springs library, with four age groups building cardboard houses, animals and cacti. The evening included dinner and games with visiting Stanford Spokes riders, then a late-night natural hot spring.
slept_at: Greg's house, Glenwood Springs CO (host)
learning_festival: Glenwood Springs public library, CO: four age groups built cardboard houses, animals and cacti. Tatiana led a Simon Says opener. The library provided lunch from a local restaurant.
contacts: Greg (host, Glenwood Springs CO)
Stanford Spokes team (visiting riders): dinner, park games and volleyball
Library team (Glenwood Springs CO): hosted the learning festival and provided lunch
planning_notes: Ask libraries about catered lunch: the Glenwood library had lunch brought in from a local restaurant one block away.
Glenwood Springs has a natural public hot spring about 10 minutes away. It is free, with a muddy bottom, while private hot springs charge about $30 for an hour.
Stanford Spokes drove 2.5 hours each way to meet the team; coordinate meetups with other Spokes teams early.
McDonald's in Glenwood Springs closes at 1am; late-night food options are limited.
Adjust cardboard projects by age: younger kids work better with a simple template and older kids can build more complex models.
